c066.title: Professor Brown's class
c066.story: It is Anna's first [[class]] this [[semester]]. Her teacher is [[Professor|professor]] Brown. He has an [[old-school]] way of teaching. He gives everyone a paper [[syllabus]]. It shows the [[curriculum]] for the year. He writes on the board with a [[marker]]. "Patience is an important [[attribute]]," he says. Then he shows them the [[campus]]. They walk to the old [[institute]] building. "It was a small [[college]] before," he says. Anna wants to be patient too.

c068.title: Small talk with exchange students
c068.story: Anna meets three exchange students from India, Ireland and Texas. Priya from India also speaks [[Hindi]]. At first, [[small talk]] is hard for Anna. There is a language [[barrier]], and everyone has a different [[accent]]. Liam uses a lot of [[slang]], and Jake speaks a southern [[dialect]]. When Jake says "Great weather!" in the rain, it is [[sarcasm]]. Liam laughs and says "Time flies," a famous [[cliché]]. Priya writes "LOL" in the chat, and Anna learns a new [[acronym]]. Liam's cousin is "between jobs," a polite [[euphemism]] for no work. Anna understands that every word can carry a [[nuance]]. "Not every Texan rides a horse," Jake says. "That is a [[stereotype]]!" By the end of the evening, they are good friends.

c069.title: Taras's math homework
c069.story: Anna's little brother Taras has [[algebra]] homework from Mrs. Koval. He is sad because it looks very hard. Anna shows him an easy [[method]]. First, they take a [[calculator]] from the drawer. They use a [[formula]] with pi. With it, they find the [[radius]] of a circle. Next, they find the [[perimeter]] of a square. After that, Taras draws a [[cube]], a [[cylinder]] and an [[oval]]. On the last page, he draws a big [[spiral]] just for fun. "Math is fun with you!" he says. The next day, he gets a top grade.

c070.title: Anna studies online
c070.story: Anna is taking an [[online course]] in marketing. Her learning app shows a thirty-day [[streak]], and she is proud. Every evening she watches a video [[tutorial]]. Each [[module]] of the [[e-learning]] program has a short quiz. For hard topics, she books one-to-one lessons on the student [[portal]]. After six weeks, she gets a [[certificate]]! Her teacher says, "You should apply for a [[grant]]." With that money, she can take a longer [[course]] at the university. Anna fills in the form that same night.

f02.title: Measuring everything at home
f02.story: Taras has a school project: measure everything at home. Anna helps him with the kitchen scale. A bag of sugar weighs one [[kilo]]. "A kilo is short for a [[kilogram]]," Anna explains. One spoon of salt weighs only ten [[grams|gram]]. Mom's vitamin pill has just fifty [[milligrams|milligram]] of iron. Next, they fill a big bottle with one [[liter]] of water. The kitchen table is almost two [[meters|meter]] long. Their walk to school is about one [[kilometer]]. Last, Taras measures an ant: just three [[millimeters|millimeter]]! His teacher loves the project and gives him a gold star.
